title: Caveman eval file
description: One eval kept as a repository file (*.eval.json) and read by cvm evals validate, run and ci. The name is the experiment: every run of the same name lines up with the last, and the gate reads a run against the experiment's saved baseline.

oneOf.description: Cases written in the file. They are kept as the dataset named like the eval.
A dataset of the project by name. Without a version its current rows are used.

A command cvm runs once per case and trial, directly and not through a shell. The case's input arrives as JSON on stdin and the output is read from stdout: JSON when it parses, else the text. A non-zero exit or a timeout is a task error, and only a task error is tried again.
Outputs already recorded in a dataset column. Cases written in the file carry theirs as `output`.

A target Caveman runs: a model, a saved prompt or an HTTP endpoint, configured as an experiment target of that kind (eval-workbench.schema.json). input_mapping names the dataset column each input is read from.
A criterion of the project's library, by name or id.
A fixed check of grader-registry.json run on each output. Every key other than type and name is one of its options.
A question the project's judge answers about each output.

gate.description: Present: a full run is compared with a baseline run of this experiment and the comparison decides the exit code. Absent: the run is reported and never compared.

baseline.description: "saved" for the experiment's saved baseline, or the id of a run of this experiment.

policy.description: statistical fails on a drop the numbers support and reads a pass on about 30 cases and more, need more data under that; strict fails when any criterion got worse on any case and decides on any number of cases. A run stores it on the experiment as its gate policy, so the console and the SDKs read a comparison by the same rule. Absent: the experiment's stored policy decides, statistical until one is stored.

budget_usd.description: The most one run may spend, at list prices.

output.description: The recorded output, read by a recorded task.
